name: Shin-Etsu Chemical Co., Ltd.
blurb: Shin-Etsu Chemical is Japan's largest chemical company and the world's leading producer of semiconductor-grade silicon wafers, holding roughly 32% of global 300-millimeter wafer capacity. It is also the world's largest producer of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and a major supplier of silicones and rare-earth magnets. The wafer division supplies the ultra-flat, ultra-pure silicon discs on which leading-edge AI chips — including Nvidia's H-series GPUs — are etched at TSMC and Samsung.
recent: In November 2025, Shin-Etsu committed ¥150 billion to expand 300mm wafer capacity at its Shirakawa and Takefu sites, targeting 2nm and 3nm node specifications. The company pioneered real-time diameter monitoring that achieves total-thickness variation below 0.09 micrometers, a threshold essential for backside power-rail designs in next-generation AI chips. AI-related wafer demand has been a bright spot even as other device categories remain weak.
